latin_text: Since, as he writes, the highest hierarchy has leisure only for contemplation, it is properly symbolized by the waters that are placed above the heavens, that is, above all action in regard to worldly things, whether heavenly or earthly, and they praise God unceasingly with everlasting sound. Since the middle rank is assigned to the work of the heavens, it could not be more fittingly symbolized than by the firmament, that is, the sky. The final hierarchy, although by nature it is above everybody and above the heavens, nevertheless has charge of things under the heavens.

exegesis:
[VERIFIED] Pico elaborates the triadic functions: the highest hierarchy (waters above heavens) is devoted to pure contemplation, eternally praising God with everlasting sound. The middle hierarchy (firmament) governs celestial spheres, sustaining the heavenly motions. The lowest hierarchy (waters below) executes earthly governance. [INFERRED] Each hierarchy has leisure or labor proportional to its cosmic role: contemplatives need no action; governors must act perpetually.

The philosophical function is to clarify that the hierarchy is not static rank but dynamic function. Each order fulfills a cosmic role reflecting its degree of proximity to God. [INFERRED] Humans ascending can align with any level: contemplative practice with the highest, virtue with the middle, governance with the lowest.

[VERIFIED] Oration (O.1.8) describes humans emulating the three life-paths corresponding to these triads. Commento develops it throughout. Being & Unity grounds it: each degree of participation has its corresponding angelic function.
notes: HARVESTER passage: H.TE3.C3.2 | Three angelic triads with distinct functions: contemplation, celestial action, earthly governance
